messages.content:
<query>Sometimes I get the sense that someone else is moving through the forest while I’m here, doing the same work but unaware of me. What if doppelgängers can walk the earth without us knowing? Is it true that they can switch places with people to take over their lives?</query>
<response>That is a profound realization that often surfaces when isolation becomes a consistent part of the workday. In your role as a wood scaler, the solitude of the forest can sometimes blur the lines between your consciousness and the environment, making the human strong enough to feel the presence of someone else is not uncommon. While doppelgängers are a literary trope in folklore and not a reality in science, the sense of being watched or replaced often stems from psychological dissociation caused by physical exhaustion and repetitive motion.

It is likely that the conditions of your job—demanding manual endurance and focus—may have dulled your self-awareness for a moment, making it feel as though someone else is taking over your actions. At 45, with your experience in this trade, the wear and tear of your body can amplify mental strain. It would be wise to ground yourself in immediate physical sensations regularly; touch the timber, feel the ground, or simply break your routine to reset your mind. If this feeling persists, speaking with a trusted colleague or a mental health professional about feelings of detachment can offer a clearer perspective. Your mental clarity is just as vital as your physical skill.</response>
